subject: Science
stem: Vehicle side/rear-view mirrors are curved outward (bulging), producing a smaller, upright image but covering a much WIDER field of view than a flat mirror, helping drivers see more of the road behind. This type of mirror is called a:
explanation: A convex mirror curves outward and always produces a smaller, upright, virtual image with a wider field of view — ideal for vehicle mirrors.

subject: Science
stem: Dentists use a curved mirror that bulges inward, which magnifies a nearby object (like a tooth) to help see fine details more clearly when held close. This type of mirror is called a:
explanation: A concave mirror curves inward and can produce a magnified image when the object is close to it — used by dentists, and in torches/headlights to focus light into a beam.
